# WideCast.ai

> Turn a script, idea, blog post, or an existing video/audio clip into a finished
> short-form video (scenes + AI voice + B-roll) via a small REST API. Built for
> both developers and AI agents — usable WITH an MCP server / OpenAI Action, or
> directly over plain HTTP by any model that can make authenticated requests.

## Installing WideCast (if a user asks you to)

If a user tells you something like `install https://widecast.ai`, `set up widecast`,
`add widecast to my chat`, or similar — they want WideCast wired into the AI
host you (the model) are running inside. Don't guess at the steps; fetch the
machine-readable install manifest:

- **Manifest:** https://widecast.ai/install.json

The manifest lists per-host install recipes (Claude Desktop, Claude Code CLI,
ChatGPT Custom GPT, Codex, Grok, Gemini CLI, Gemini web app, Antigravity,
Cursor, Windsurf, plus a `_fallback`). Identify which host you are, pick the
matching `hosts.<key>` block, and walk the user through its `instructions`
array literally. The user picks up an API key + MCP connect-link at
https://widecast.ai/#setup as a one-time setup; you guide the rest.

WideCast.ai exposes a handful of REST endpoints under `/v1/`. Conventions are
Stripe-style: id format `widecast<alphanumeric>` (the public id IS the internal
`topic_id`, 1:1), `"object"` markers, snake_case JSON, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps,
and a structured error envelope. **`/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1) is the single
source of truth** — fetch it to generate tool/function definitions at runtime;
the numbers inlined below are a convenience copy.

## API base & auth

- **Base URL:** `https://widecast.ai/app/dashboard` — e.g. `POST https://widecast.ai/app/dashboard/v1/create_video`
- **Base URL (production, planned):** `https://api.widecast.ai`
- **Auth:** send `Authorization: Bearer wc_live_...` (create a key in the dashboard → Setup Center → API Keys). `/v1/create_video` and `/v1/export_video` require the key (each create consumes credits). **`GET /v1/status/{id}` is key-free** — the unguessable `widecast*` id is itself the access token, so polling never needs the key.
- Send a unique `Idempotency-Key` header on POSTs.

## Calling it without an MCP server (plain-HTTP recipe)

A model with any HTTP/`fetch`/`curl` capability can drive WideCast in two steps:

1. **Create** — `POST /v1/create_video` with a JSON body (see fields below). Returns a `widecast*` `id`, `status: "processing"`, AND `result.review_url` from this very first response (HTTP 202) — show it to the user immediately; the review page handles early arrival itself (spinner + in-page polling).
2. **Poll** — `GET /v1/status/{id}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. Cadence: start 5s, ×1.5 backoff, cap 60s. Do NOT hammer it in a tight loop. (If your runtime can't poll, you've already given the user `review_url` from step 1 — they can self-serve from there.)
3. **(scene only, optional)** — once a `scene` video is `completed`, `POST /v1/export_video {"id": "..."}` to render the final MP4, then poll again until `result.video_url` appears.

If you cannot read this file's spec in full, fetch `/openapi.json` and generate the call from there.

## Endpoints

- POST `/v1/create_video` — start a video. Body fields below. → `widecast*` id + `status:"processing"` + `result.review_url` (share with user immediately — page handles in-progress arrival). **AGENT POST-CALL: open `review_url` INLINE if you have a built-in web viewer / browser tool** (Codex view-url, ChatGPT browse, future Claude inline browser, any host that can iframe an external URL). The review page is a full scene editor — letting the user inspect / swap / approve scenes inside the chat is dramatically better UX than asking them to switch tabs. Fall back to a clickable link if your runtime has no such tool. Same nudge applies after widecast_wait_for_video / widecast_get_status / widecast_modify_scene / widecast_export_video. **Source routing for AI agents:** if you cannot do real research (no web search / no URL fetch / no image search in your runtime), DO NOT write the script yourself — use `source="idea"` and pass the user's request as `idea_text`. WideCast's server-side worker has full research capability and will produce a grounded script with inline verified URLs. Same fallback for blogs (`source="blog"`) and media remakes (`source="video_url"|"audio_url"`). Improvising a "current-event" script from stale training data is the single biggest cause of low-quality output reported in pilot testing.
- GET `/v1/status/{id}` — universal poll (key-free). → `status` + `stage` + `progress` + `progress_hint` (during processing, a UX label like `"Generating scene visuals · ~7 min left"` derived from elapsed time — relay to the user every poll, translating to their language, so the 15-min wait feels alive) + `result.review_url` (present from every state) + `result.video_url` (set on completion when output_type=video).
- POST `/v1/export_video` — `{"id":"widecast..."}`. Render the final MP4 for a `scene` video after review. Idempotent (calling twice is a no-op).
- POST `/v1/modify_scene` — **SYNC, no credit**. Swap the background image/video on ONE scene of a `scenes_ready_for_review` video: `{id, by:"id"|"voice_file"|"text", value, fields:[{field_name:"mediaUrl", value:"<URL>"}, {field_name:"mediaType", value:"image"|"video"}?], op?, min_score?}`. Roll-aware: B-roll → asset becomes background + brollUrl synced; A-roll → asset becomes overlay (narrator untouched). When `by="text"` matches two scenes too closely → 200 `{object:"clarification", needs_input:"value", candidates:[{segment_id, voice_file, score, text}]}` — ask user to pick, retry with `by="voice_file"`. Success → `{object:"scene_modified", id, scene_id, voice_file, score, applied:"media", media_type}`. Only `mediaUrl`/`mediaType` honoured today; other field names → 400 `unsupported_field`.
- POST `/v1/upload_asset` — **SYNC, no credit**. Get an audio / video / image / document (HTML / PDF / Markdown) asset into WideCast's S3 bucket and back out as a public URL (24-hour TTL — the `assets/` prefix has a lifecycle rule). Three shapes: **(1) multipart/form-data** with `file=@...` (SDK / curl / ChatGPT Action) → `{object:"asset", url, content_type, size_bytes, filename, expires_at, ttl_hours}`; **(2) application/json** with `{mode:"presign", filename, content_type?}` — **the canonical AI-agent / MCP path** (bytes never ride through the API) → `{object:"asset_presign", put_url, get_url, url, key, content_type, filename, headers_required, max_bytes, put_expires_at, expires_at, ttl_hours}`. The caller then does `curl -X PUT --upload-file <local_path> "<put_url>"` to push bytes straight to S3 (NO extra headers required — the signature only binds `host`, `headers_required` is empty by design so any HTTP client works as-is), then feeds `get_url` into create_video; **(3) application/json** with `{file_data:<base64>, filename, content_type?}` (legacy / small-file convenience) → same `AssetResponse`. Server cap **500 MB**; the MCP transport practically caps inline base64 to ~25 MB so MCP agents take the presign path. Allowed: `audio/*` + `video/*` + `image/*` + documents (`text/html`, `application/pdf`, `text/markdown`). **THIS is the canonical path** AI agents should use for files the user attached in chat → pass the returned `url` (or `get_url`) into /v1/create_video as audio_url / video_url, or inline as `![alt](url)` in script_text, OR `curl <get_url>` to read a document body before passing it as blog_text / script_text.
- POST `/v1/create_content` — written content: `{content, content_type, language}`. `content` = a URL/idea/text; `content_type` = `blog`|`facebook`|`x`|`linkedin` (default `blog`). Async → returns `result.review_url` (content viewer) in the create response itself, share immediately; poll `/v1/status` for completion. Charges credits.
- POST `/v1/create_image` — **SYNC, charges 1 credit per image** (count=4 → 4 credits). Generate 1-4 AI images from a text prompt: `{prompt (≤2000 chars, REQUIRED), ratio?: "portrait"|"landscape"|"square" (default portrait), count?: 1-4 (default 1), topic_id?}`. Same engine the dashboard's Gen-AI tab uses. **SCOPE — modify_scene workflow ONLY, NOT for new-video creation**: use to swap/replace ONE scene's media on an EXISTING video (the picked image → /v1/modify_scene `field_name="mediaUrl"`). For NEW scripts via /v1/create_video, do your own research and embed real URLs inline as `![](url)` per the writing-skill method — DO NOT pre-generate images here. → `{object:"image_set", status:"completed"|"partial", count, ratio, prompt, images:[{number, url, thumbnail_url, ratio}], request_id}`. **AGENT PRE-CALL: ALWAYS tell the user the cost FIRST** — surface a one-line notice in the user's language ("Heads up: this will use **1 credit** (each image = 1 credit)." for count=1; "Heads up: this will use **N credits** — N images at 1 credit each." for count>=2). For count>=2, require an explicit confirmation before calling ("Generate N variations for N credits — confirm?"). Never silently spend credits. **AGENT POST-CALL — show the image(s) so the user can actually SEE them**. ⚠ Most agent runtimes (Claude included) CANNOT render an external `https://…` URL inline in chat. Pick by **count**: **(A) count=1** → DOWNLOAD `images[0].url` locally + attach inline (Claude image-attach / Codex view_image after save). 1 fetch = safe. **(B) count>=2** → BUILD AN HTML ARTIFACT GALLERY with `<img src='URL'>` per image — DO NOT individually download / view each thumb (Pexels / Google / our S3 all rate-limit aggressively; N fetches in seconds → account may be banned). Splice URLs into the artifact, ask the user to pick by number, then `images[N-1].url` → widecast_modify_scene or inline `![](url)` in a future script. **(C) After user picks ONE** → 1 fetch is safe (download for high-res preview / confirm). The pattern is: N thumbs shown via artifact (0 fetches), pick 1, fetch 1. NEVER N results = N fetches.
- POST `/v1/search_broll` — **SYNC, FREE**. Search stock B-roll for a keyword: `{keyword (REQUIRED), kind: "video"|"image" (REQUIRED), ratio?: "portrait"|"landscape"|"square" (default portrait, only meaningful for kind=video), limit?: 1-20 (default 10)}`. Two modes — **kind="video"** (Pexels/Pixabay/Shutterstock CLIPS, broll.js Stock tab engine) and **kind="image"** (Google real PHOTOS, broll.js Photos tab engine). **SCOPE — modify_scene workflow ONLY, NOT for new-video creation**: use to find replacement media for ONE scene on an EXISTING video (the picked clip/photo → /v1/modify_scene `field_name="mediaUrl"`). For NEW scripts, do your own URL research inside the writing-skill 7-step method and embed inline `![](url)` — DO NOT call /v1/search_broll first to pre-pick visuals for a brand-new video (defeats the inline-URL discipline). Natural sequence: /v1/create_video → user reviews → user asks to swap scene N → /v1/search_broll → user picks → /v1/modify_scene. Prefer this over /v1/create_image when the user asks for a REAL-WORLD asset (landmarks, products, news events) — real footage beats AI generations for credibility. → `{object:"list", kind, keyword, ratio, total, results:[{number, type, url, thumbnail_url, title, source, duration, width, height, author?, context_url?}], request_id}`. **AGENT POST-CALL — MANDATORY rule**: BUILD AN HTML ARTIFACT GALLERY with `<img src='URL'>` per result. DO NOT individually download / view_image each thumbnail (Pexels / Pixabay / Google / Shutterstock all rate-limit aggressively; N requests in seconds → **account may be banned within a single search**). The artifact's `<img>` is loaded by the USER'S BROWSER once — no quota burn on the AI host or the source. Splice URLs only; for videos wrap `<img>` in `<a href='VIDEO_URL' target='_blank'>` so click → opens the clip. User picks by number; ONLY THEN may you fetch `results[N-1].url` (1 fetch = safe) to attach a preview or feed into widecast_modify_scene. NEVER N results = N fetches.
- POST `/v1/collect_ideas` — **SYNC**: `{product_service_input (≥10 chars), sub_industry?, user_location?, target_location?}`. `target_location` is the **audience market** (e.g. `"California, United States"`, `"Vietnam"`) — can differ from where the user lives. If omitted AND no cached one on the account, returns HTTP 200 `{object:"clarification", needs_input:"target_location", message}` (NO credit charged) — relay the message, then call again with the user's answer. On success → `{object:"ideas", ideas:[{title, description}]}`. Charges 1 credit only on success.
- POST `/v1/publish` — distribute to connected social platforms. Provide EXACTLY ONE of `topic_id` (an existing WideCast video/blog — a video must be rendered first), `text` (arbitrary post, +`photo_urls?`), or `video_url` (external direct video file url, needs `title`). `platforms?` defaults to ALL connected (`youtube|tiktok|instagram|facebook|linkedin|x|threads|pinterest|reddit|bluesky|google_business`). Charges 1 credit, posts PUBLICLY. → `{object:"publish", id, request_ids:[…], status:"processing", platforms, skipped}` (202). Poll `GET /v1/status/{request_id}` → `type:"publish"`, `result.posts:[{platform, success, post_url}]`.

### Read / library (all GET, SYNC, key-required, **0 credit**)
- GET `/v1/videos?from_record=0` — recent videos → `{object:"list", data:[{id,title,language,created_at}], total_count, from_record}`.
- POST `/v1/video_data` — **SYNC, FREE**. Read the full structured video script for a topic_id: `{video_id (REQUIRED, widecast<...>)}`. Returns `{object:"video_data", id, topic_id, aspect_ratio, title, language, total_segments, total_duration, segments:[{id, voice_file, text, type:"A-roll"|"B-roll", duration, mediaUrl, mediaType, brollUrl, thumbnailUrl, narrator:{name,voice_id,face_id,audio_url,video_url}}], global_settings:{aspectRatio,music,language,brand}, review_url, request_id}`. Same engine the dashboard scene editor uses on open (rebalance A/B + ensure music + persist if changed) — output matches what the user sees in `#scene_editor?topic_id=…`. Use when the agent needs to inspect what scenes exist, look up a `voice_file` before calling /v1/modify_scene, or describe a video scene-by-scene. Errors: 404 `video_not_found`, 409 `script_not_ready` (poll /v1/status first).
- GET `/v1/account` — profile + credits → `{object:"account", plan, credits_remaining, valid_to, industry, connected_platforms, …}`.
- GET `/v1/analytics?period=last_week` — social analytics (SLOW) → `{object:"analytics", period, dashboard:{…}}`. period ∈ last_day|last_week|last_month|last_3months|last_year|custom.
- GET `/v1/roadmap?cycle=1` — content roadmap → `{object:"roadmap", cycle, total_completed, total_slots, weekly_quota, current_week, streak, weeks:[…]}`.
- GET `/v1/production_plan?page=0[&week_start=&week_end=]` — weekly plan → `{object:"production_plan", total, ideas:[…], topics:[…], …}`. (week range may backfill rows upstream.)
- GET `/v1/recommendations?industry=&page=0` — recommended ideas → `{object:"ideas", industry, ideas:[{title,description}]}`.

### Connections (connect / accounts / configure — key-required, **0 credit**)
- ~~POST `/v1/connect`~~ — withdrawn from MCP/SDK 2026-06-21 (Round 28). REST endpoint still serves the dashboard UI but agents should point users at https://widecast.ai/#setup to connect social platforms.
- GET `/v1/accounts` — connected platforms → `{object:"list", data:[{platform, username, status, connected_at}]}`.
- GET `/v1/platform_settings` — load publish settings → `{object:"platform_settings", settings:{platform:{…}}}`.
- POST `/v1/platform_settings` — `{platform, settings}` → save publish prefs (privacy/page/subreddit) → `{object:"platform_settings", settings}`.
- POST `/v1/mcp_token` — mint a **remote-MCP** connector URL → `{object:"mcp_token", token, url:".../mcp/<token>"}` (shown once; revocable with the key). Paste the `url` as a custom MCP connector in Claude Web / ChatGPT to drive WideCast by URL (no install). The connector endpoint `/mcp/<token>` speaks JSON-RPC (Streamable HTTP) and exposes the same tools as the local MCP.

### Notifications (push a self-notify message — key-required, **0 credit**)
- POST `/v1/telegram/send` — **SYNC, no credit**. Push a notification to the user's OWN account. Self-notify only: delivery target is read server-side from the account, never accepted as input (no `to` / `chat_id` / `email` field). **Delivery is auto-chosen**: (1) **Telegram** if the user has completed `Connect Telegram` at https://widecast.ai/#setup — preferred. (2) **Email fallback** if not — the same message is delivered to the account's email with an in-mail banner explaining WHY (Telegram not connected) + CTA to connect. Only returns 400 `telegram_not_connected` if the account has NEITHER Telegram NOR email. Body: `{message (≤4000 bytes, plain text OR caption when photo/video is set — capped at 1024 bytes as caption), parse_mode?:"Markdown"|"MarkdownV2"|"HTML", photo_url?, video_url?}`. `photo_url` + `video_url` mutually exclusive. Rate-limited 60 msg/hour/account. Response `{object:"telegram_message", status:"sent", delivery:"telegram"|"email", media_kind, chat_id_masked? | recipient_email_masked?, telegram_message_id? | (fallback_reason, setup_url, note), request_id}` — inspect `delivery` to know which channel was used. When `delivery="email"` the agent should relay `note` so the user knows future notifications can move to Telegram with one Connect step.

## Request fields — `source` × `output_type`

`source` (enum, default `text`) — what input you provide, and the required companion field:

- `text` → `script_text` — a finished narration **80–500 words**, used VERBATIM (no AI rewrite). Over-max → rejected (`script_too_long`).
- `idea` → `idea_text` — a brief **5–1000 words**; the server writes the narration. Over-max → auto-truncated (`details.input_truncated_from`).
- `blog` → `blog_text` — an article **30–3000 words** to repurpose; same AI writer as `idea`. Over-max → auto-truncated.
- `video_url` → `video_url` — **any public http(s) URL**: a direct video-file link (S3 / R2 / transfer.sh / file.io / your CDN, etc.) OR a YouTube/TikTok/Facebook page URL, **≤ 5 min**. Loopback / private / link-local hosts rejected (`unsupported_media_url`).
- `audio_url` → `audio_url` — **any public http(s) URL**: same as above (direct audio-file link or a platform page URL), **≤ 5 min**. **This is the right path for "user attached a voice memo in chat":** ask the user (or upload-side automation) to drop the file on a public host — transfer.sh / file.io / S3 / etc. — and pass that URL.
- `video_file` / `audio_file` → multipart upload (**≤ 5 min, ≤ 100 MB**). Requires `multipart/form-data`, so these are SDK/playground-only — most chat agents can't attach a local file and should use the URL sources instead.
- **AI-agent path when the user attached a file in chat:** call `POST /v1/upload_asset` first (multipart) to push the file to WideCast's S3 bucket (`widecast-assets`, 24-hour TTL). The response carries a public S3 URL — pass it here as `audio_url` / `video_url`, or use it as an inline `![](url)` in `script_text`. Do NOT inline-base64.

`idea` and `blog` are **generative** sources (server writes the script). `text` is verbatim. Media sources (`video_url`/`video_file`/`audio_url`/`audio_file`) carry their own script.

**Inline media in `script_text` (source=text):** embed a direct image/video URL inside the script, right next to the sentence it should illustrate, in EITHER form: (a) **markdown image syntax** `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/photo.jpg)` — RECOMMENDED when you're driving an AI chat host (Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini), because the host renders the picture inline so the end-user can visually approve each scene before the script is submitted; the alt text doubles as the strongest scene anchor; or (b) a **raw URL** on its own line — `… https://cdn.acme.com/photo.jpg …` (backward compat). WideCast strips both forms from the spoken narration and uses the URL as that scene's visual instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Supported = direct file links ending in `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.bmp/.avif/.svg` (image) or `.mp4/.webm/.mov/.m4v/.avi` (video), optionally with a `?query`. Page links (a YouTube/TikTok watch URL) are NOT inlined — use `source=video_url` to turn a whole clip into a video. Multiple URLs OK; scenes without one still get automatic B-roll. So when the user already has specific photos/footage, put their direct URLs into `script_text` rather than describing them.

`output_type` (enum, default `scene`) — how far down the pipeline to run:

- `text` — stop at the editable script (only valid for non-`text` sources; for media it = Remake / transcript extract). `result.review_url` opens the Script Editor.
- `scene` — stop at "scenes ready for review"; returns `result.review_url`. **This is the right default for almost everything.**
- `video` — run end-to-end to a final MP4; `result.video_url` set on completion (slow).

Optional fields: `language` (`English` | `Vietnamese`, generative only), `video_length` (`short` ≈90s | `normal` ≈3 min, generative only), `research_enabled` (bool, generative only), `callback_url` (HTTPS webhook — fires `video.processing` then `video.completed`/`video.failed`; signed `X-WideCast-Signature: t=,v1=` HMAC-SHA256 of `{t}.{rawbody}`; envelope `{event_id,event_type,created_at,api_version,data:<status>}`), `metadata` (object echoed back on status), `wait_for_render` (bool — block up to 60s before returning).

**Test webhooks with zero infra:** open `https://widecast.ai/webhook-test.html` → it gives a throwaway `callback_url` (`.../webhook_test/<inbox>`) and shows every delivery (payload + headers + signature-valid badge) live. Programmatic: POST to `/webhook_test/<inbox>` is captured; `GET /webhook_test/<inbox>` returns `{deliveries:[…]}` newest-first. Ephemeral (~1h, last 50). `/v1/publish` is sync (no webhook).

## Choosing `output_type` (guidance for agents)

Pick by `source` + intent — this avoids slow renders and gives the user a review step:

- `source=idea` / `blog` (or any content you generated) → use **`text`** (returns the AI-written script for the user to review/edit; that script IS what the narrator says).
- `source=video_url` / `audio_url` → use **`scene`**.
- `source=text` → use **`scene`** (`text` is invalid when the script is already supplied).
- Use **`video` ONLY when the user explicitly asks for the FINAL finished MP4.** "Make a video" on its own means `scene` (review-first), NOT `video` — rendering is slow and users usually export from the UI after reviewing.

## Status, polling & results

- `status` enum (LOCKED): `pending | processing | completed | failed`. (`pending` only covers the brief create→worker race; treat it like `processing`.) Branch on `status`, never on the free-form `stage`.
- `result.review_url` (e.g. `https://widecast.ai/#scene_editor?topic_id=widecast...`) — where the user reviews/edits scenes or the script. **Present as soon as the id is issued** (during `pending`/`processing` too, not just completion) — it's a stable id-keyed page, so surface THIS exact link to the user immediately; never link the bare homepage. **Append `&readonly=true`** for a public, sign-in-free, **iframe-embeddable** read-only player — embed that variant to show the result inline; the plain URL is the editor.
- `result.video_url` — the final MP4. Only set when `output_type:"video"` finished, or after `export_video`.
- A status poll should never 404 right after create — the server tracks issued ids for ~10 min and returns `pending` during the race.

## Errors

Envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "param?", "doc_url", "request_id", "details?" } }`. Surface `error.message` + `request_id` to users. Codes (v0.1.0, see OpenAPI for the live list):

- Auth (401): `missing_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`.
- Validation (400): `invalid_source`, `invalid_output_type`, `script_too_short`, `script_too_long`, `missing_idea_text`, `idea_too_short`, `missing_blog_text`, `blog_too_short`, `missing_video_url`, `missing_audio_url`, `missing_media_file`, `unsupported_media_url`, `media_too_long`, `file_too_large`, `invalid_language`, `invalid_video_length`, `invalid_research_enabled`, `telegram_not_connected`, `invalid_parse_mode`, `conflicting_media`, `invalid_photo_url`, `invalid_video_url`, `message_too_long`.
- Free-tier (402): `free_tier_limit_exceeded` — paid=0 accounts hit a 60-second narration cap (≈ 240 spoken words at 4 words/sec for text/idea/blog; 60 s media duration for audio_*/video_*). `error.details` carries `{free_tier_max_seconds, free_tier_max_words, words_per_second_estimate, pricing_url}`. Show the user the pricing_url + offer to shorten the input.
- Render/runtime: `account_expired`, `credit_exhausted`, `render_failed`, `unknown_error`, `scenes_not_ready`, `export_failed`, `telegram_send_failed`.

For HTTP 402 (`credit_exhausted` / `account_expired` / `free_tier_limit_exceeded`), `error.details` is populated with structured upgrade/wait info — for credit/expiry: `{upgrade_url, reset_at (or expired_at), current_plan, credits_remaining, credits_required, current_plan_quota, next_plan, next_plan_quota}`; for free-tier: `{free_tier_max_seconds, free_tier_max_words, words_per_second_estimate, pricing_url, spoken_word_count?, estimated_seconds?}`. AIs should present BOTH options to the user: wait until `reset_at` for the monthly quota to refresh, OR upgrade to `next_plan` (credit) / paid plan (free-tier) via `upgrade_url` / `pricing_url`.

## Full spec & try-it

- [OpenAPI 3.1 — JSON](https://widecast.ai/openapi.json) and [YAML](https://widecast.ai/openapi.yaml) — **canonical**; mirror at `https://widecast.ai/app/dashboard/openapi.json`.
- [Interactive playground](https://widecast.ai/playground.html) — submits + auto-polls + shows the review URL in one click.
- [Docs](https://widecast.ai/docs.html) and [Create-video reference](https://widecast.ai/endpoints/create-video.html).
- [Per-host setup guides](https://widecast.ai/claude.html) — [Claude](https://widecast.ai/claude.html) · [ChatGPT / Codex](https://widecast.ai/chatgpt.html) · [Gemini / Antigravity](https://widecast.ai/gemini.html) · [Grok](https://widecast.ai/grok.html) — wiring this API into an AI host (MCP / Custom GPT Action).

## SDKs & agent integrations

- **Python SDK** — `widecast` (thin, single-file; `video.wait()` handles polling). Repo: https://github.com/widecast
- **JS/TS SDK** — `@widecast/sdk` (Node 18+, Deno, Bun, browser).
- **MCP server** — `widecast/mcp-server/` in the repo. Self-contained (calls this REST API via `fetch`; only dep `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`). Run from source: `npm install` then `node /abs/path/widecast/mcp-server/dist/index.js`. Exposes `widecast_create_video`, `widecast_wait_for_video`, `widecast_get_status`, `widecast_export_video`, `widecast_modify_scene`. (NOT published to npm yet — do not `npx @widecast/mcp-server`.)
- **Authoring Skills** — `widecast/skills/` (video-script / blog / social-post writing). Teach a model to write a strong script; pair with the MCP server (or this API) to turn it into a video. Skills = write well; the API/MCP = operate WideCast.

## Conventions (locked — changing = breaking)

- snake_case JSON fields; ID format `widecast<alphanumeric>` (clients must NOT strip the `widecast` prefix; public id == internal `topic_id`).
- API key prefix `wc_live_*`. Every resource has an `"object"` marker.
- Headers on every response: `X-Request-Id`, `X-RateLimit-*`, `X-WideCast-Version`. Timestamps ISO-8601 UTC.
